references.text: Describes the anointing of Aaron as high priest by pouring anointing oil over his head, which is the same ritual mentioned in Leviticus 21:10
Refers to the holy garments made for Aaron as high priest, corresponding to 'putting on the garments' in Leviticus 21:10
Concerns the consecration of the high priest and his garments, which corresponds to 'filling his hand' (consecration) in Leviticus 21:10
Describes how Moses poured anointing oil over Aaron's head to sanctify him, a direct parallel to the anointing mentioned in Leviticus 21:10
Prohibits Aaron from showing grief by letting his hair hang loose or tearing his clothes because of the anointing oil, the same prohibition found in Leviticus 21:10
Refers to letting the hair grow freely (the same Hebrew word 'para') in connection with the Nazirite vow, which contrasts with the prohibition for the high priest
Poetic description of the anointing oil running down over Aaron's head and beard, a reference to priestly anointing
The prophet Ezekiel is forbidden from performing common mourning rituals such as letting his hair hang loose, corresponding to the rules for the high priest
Describes Jesus as the perfect high priest who is holy, innocent, and exalted, and who was appointed by oath forever
